Sections Accessibility Audit VPAT/ACR Technical Support User Testing Document Remediation Accessibility Certification Accessibility Audit Cost Accessible.org web accessibility audits cost $100 – $250 per page (or screen) and $25 – $100 for light pages/screens. Our audits follow best practices for ADA and EAA compliance. Our audit price is based on comprehensive manual evaluation using the WCAG 2.1 AA standard (or WCAG 2.2 AA). Audits are conducted in desktop environment with the client option to add mobile. Our website accessibility audits are fully manual, formal evaluations conducted by technical accessibility experts who evaluate your website or other digital assets against WCAG 2.0 AA, WCAG 2.1 AA, or WCAG 2.2 AA standards. Scope typically does not include all pages or screens, but rather a representative sample. We use an automated scan as a review to ensure all issues correctly identified by a scan are included in our final audit report. All Accessible.org auditors are certified DHS Trusted Testers. The DHS Trusted Tester Process is a manual test approach that aligns with the ICT Testing Baseline, and provides repeatable and reliable conformance test results. Digital Assets Audited Accessible.org can audit all types of digital assets: Websites Web pages Web apps Mobile apps Platforms Dashboards Software Games Widgets Elements Components Portals Multimedia Players Evaluation Methodology Accessible.org uses the following methodologies and environments when evaluating your digital asset(s): Screen Reader Testing Keyboard Testing Visual Inspection Code Inspection Automated Scan: AXE Color Contrast Analyzer Tool Browser Zoom: 200% 400% Assistive Technologies: Screen Readers: NVDA, JAWS, and/or VoiceOver. Browser Environments: Browsers: Chrome and Safari. Operating Systems: Windows (desktop) iOS (mobile) Device Environments: Audit includes desktop environment with client option to add mobile (iPhone). By choosing our audit services, you will receive an excellent quality, easy to understand audit report that your team can take action on. We can add other environments (e.g., MacOS and Android) upon request for an additional fee. Our website accessibility audit cost breakdown shows you exactly how we determine your final audit price quote. Price: $350 for the WCAG VPAT version. User testing is conducted by an accessibility professional with a disability, is an essential part of ensuring your digital assets are accessible to all users. We offer user testing at a discounted rate when combined with our audit and remediation services. Service Details: User Testing : Conducted by a professional who is blind or visually impaired, using screen reader assistive technology to evaluate your website or digital asset. Deliverable : You will receive a recording of the user testing session upon completion. Deliverables: Recording of the user testing session upon completion. User Testing Attestation Note : User testing sessions include up to 10 pages or screens with a time duration cap of 30 minutes. Price $550 per session $450 per session if you choose us for audit services. Email us [email protected] Accessibility Remediation Cost We will remediate your digital asset at the code level. This means we will fix the technically complex accessibility issues on your website, web app, or mobile app. To be eligible for remediation, we must 1) audit your digital asset and 2) have full code access. The audit is necessary to ensure we know all accessibility issues that exist (we don’t accept outside audits to uphold quality). Full code access is necessary to ensure we’re able to make all fixes. We validate our remediation. Service Details: Remediation : Conducted by a technical accessibility expert with development experience. All fixed issues are reviewed and validated by auditor. Deliverable : You will receive your code remediated digital asset. Remediation Includes: Technical code remediation Validation of remediation Note: An audit and full code access is required for remediation. Price $750 – $4,500 for most clients, $100 – $450 per page or screen, depending on volume and complexity. Email us [email protected] Document Remediation Cost Document accessibility remediation costs start at $4.00 per page. The price of remediating PDFs, Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, and Excel spreadsheets for WCAG 2.1 AA conformance depends on the document status and project scope. We will remediate your documents to meet the highest accessibility standards including WCAG 2.1 / 2.2 AA and PDF/UA standards. Documents include: Microsoft PowerPoint documents PDFs Microsoft Word documents Microsoft Excel spreadsheets Canva documents We will manually test documents and fix accessibility issues according to WCAG 2.1 AA and WCAG 2.2 AA standards and PDF/UA. Large Projects : $7,500 to $10,000+ Our prices are determined by the size of the project. Email us [email protected] Consulting Kris brings 7 years of accessibility and compliance experience to every session. Kris has worked with hundreds of clients from Fortune 500 companies to local governments to small businesses. Kris’s insight and strategy can help your organization save hundreds of hours of time and hundreds of thousands of dollars. Our technical experts have years of experience in accessibility and can provide the immediate answers and knowledge your team is looking for. Price Kris Rivenburgh: $495 Technical Accessibility Experts: $195 Email us [email protected] Frequently Asked Questions How much does a website accessibility audit cost? Most website accessibility audits range between $1,250 and $2,750. Pricing is $100 to $250 per primary page or screen and $25 to $100 for light pages or screens. Because our audits are custom and fully manual, your final cost depends on scope, status, and complexity. How is the audit price determined? Three factors set the price: scope (the number and type of pages or screens in your representative sample), status (how accessible the asset already is), and complexity (interactive components, dynamic content, and custom widgets). We evaluate a representative sample rather than every page. What is the difference between a primary page and a light page? Primary pages are content rich or interactive pages and screens, priced at $100 to $250 each. Light pages have minimal content or repeated patterns and are priced lower, at $25 to $100 each. Light pages can be simple pages like a privacy policy page or simple How much does an ACR cost? Most clients choose our WCAG edition VPAT service, which is $350 in addition to the cost of the audit. We complete the Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) and produce a finished Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) based on the audit. Other editions are Section 508 at $550, EN 301 549 at $650, and the INT combined edition at $950. The different amounts represent the time necessary to fill out the different editions. What WCAG standards do you evaluate against? We evaluate digital assets against WCAG 2.1 AA or WCAG 2.2 AA, and occasionally WCAG 2.0 AA. Are your audits manual or automated? Fully manual. There is no such thing as an automated audit. Our technical accessibility experts will evaluate your asset using screen reader testing (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, and/or TalkBack), keyboard testing, visual inspection, and code inspection. We use an automated scan only as a review, to confirm that every scan detectable issue is included in the final audit report. What do I receive at the end of an audit? A detailed technical audit report delivered as an Excel spreadsheet, with specific findings, the WCAG criteria affected, and the information your team needs to take action on each issue. Do you fix the issues you find? We can support remediation in two ways. Technical support, at $195 per hour with a two hour minimum, gives your team expert help and validates fixes (to ensure the fix has resolved the issue). Document remediation, starting at $7.00 per page, covers PDFs, Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, and Excel spreadsheets. How much does document remediation cost? Document remediation starts at $7.00 per page. PDFs start at $7.50 per page, while Word documents and PowerPoint presentations start at $7.00 per page. Final pricing depends on document status and project scope. Do you offer rush or expedited service? Yes. Expedited accessibility, including same day or overnight turnaround, ranges from $250 to $750 depending on scope and timing. Is certification an extra cost? No. Certification is included at no additional cost as a result of our services. To qualify for a statement of conformance or certification, your asset must be fully WCAG conformant. A statement of partial conformance is available when the only remaining issues are outside your control. Can you audit mobile apps and other digital assets? Yes. We audit websites, web apps, mobile apps, software, platforms, dashboards, portals, multimedia players, and individual components. Audits can be conducted in desktop and/or mobile environments. Do you offer user testing with people with disabilities? Yes. User testing is conducted by an accessibility professional with a disability using assistive technology, and the session is recorded for your team. Sessions are $550, or $450 when combined with audit services, and cover up to 10 pages or screens. How do I get a quote or get started? Email [email protected] or use our contact page. You can also try our cost calculator for a fast estimate. Ready to Start? We’re ready to help you with accessibility as soon as possible. We provide upfront quotes, clear expectations, and fast turnarounds. Send us a message and we’ll reply very soon. Low-content books are generally repetitive, and designed to be filled in by the user. This does not typically include activity books, such as puzzle books or coloring books, which generally do not feature repetitive content on each page. See common examples of low-content books in the table below, but note that there can be exceptions. Reviews for low-content books and for activity books, such as coloring or puzzle books, might take 3-4 weeks. To check review times, visit Timelines . Low-content books do not require an ISBN. If you want an ISBN for your low-content book, you can use your own ISBN, or publish without an ISBN. Low-content books are not eligible for the free KDP ISBN. See the differences between using your own ISBN and publishing without an ISBN below. Note: we don't currently offer Release Date for low-content books. How to create a low-content book Creating a low-content book is similar to creating other print books, but your ISBN options are different as noted in the steps below. To publish a low-content book: Go to your Bookshelf . Click + Create new title or series and then select Create paperback or Create hardcover . Enter your information for each section as follows: Paperback or Hardcover details. Enter your title, description, keywords, etc. Under Categories you need to check the Low-content box. Please note that if you do not select this box, or select a different box, your book will be rejected. Paperback or Hardcover content. Under Print ISBN , you can choose between Publish without an ISBN or Use my own ISBN . Upload your manuscript and cover files, preview your book, and order a proof. Paperback or Hardcover rights and pricing. Choose the territories where you hold distribution rights and set your list price. After entering your information, click Publish Your Paperback Book or Publish Your Hardcover Book. See more detailed instructions on creating a book . Hardcover publishing is not supported on kdp.amazon.co.jp. What type of barcode will appear on a low-content book? If you use your own ISBN, you can upload a cover with or without a barcode. If you choose the option Publish without an ISBN , or decide not to provide your own barcode, we'll automatically place one on your back cover. We'll place a barcode in a 2" (50.8 mm) by 1.2" (30.5 mm) white box in the lower right-hand corner of your book's back cover. If you leave images or text on this part of the cover, the barcode will cover them during printing, which could result in your file being rejected, so don't include any text or objects in this area. Low-content books that are published without an ISBN are not eligible for Transparency codes. Note: Transparency codes are being retired from KDP print barcodes and are not available for books created after November 2025. Learn more about barcodes . What information can be updated after publishing a low-content book? After publishing your book, certain features are locked. Learn more about the changes that can be made after publishing . Changing your ISBN option You cannot change your ISBN selection after you've published your book. If you need to change your ISBN selection after publishing your book, you'll need to unpublish your book from your KDP Bookshelf, and then republish it. See more about unpublishing a book . Expanded Distribution Expanded Distribution is not supported for low-content books, regardless of the ISBN option you select. Learn more about enrollment requirements . Read Sample (Look Inside the Book) feature The sample and the back cover thumbnail are currently not supported for low-content books published without ISBN. If you'd like to activate this feature for your book, we recommend you to buy your own ISBN from Bowker or through your local ISBN agency. Learn more about using your own ISBN . Alternatively, you can use A+ Content to add images of your book's interior so buyers can see what it looks like. These images will appear on your book detail page. Learn more about A+ Content . Series Low-content books are not eligible for creating a series, regardless of the ISBN option you select. Learn more about series . Yes, they are. We've updated the product names, but these are the same formats previously referred to as Blurb Trade Books . "Trade book" is an industry term for standard-format paperback and hardcover books—commonly used by self-publishers and traditional publishers alike to create books for general audiences. What is the difference between hardcover and paperback books? Hardcover books are bound with hard, protective covers and are typically more durable and premium-looking. Paperback books have flexible, soft covers and are lighter and more cost-effective. Our hardcover books are available with an ImageWrap hardcover or a Linen hardcover with a dust jacket. Our paperback books are available with an ImageWrap softcover. What type of book can I make? Paperback and hardcover books are ideal for projects with a mix of images and words, or just words alone, including novels, memoirs, poetry collections, journals, notebooks, children’s books, how-to-guides and more. What is the page limit for a paperback or hardcover book? A paperback or hardcover book must have a minimum of 24 pages and a maximum of 480 pages. How much does it cost to make a paperback book with Blurb? The cost of a paperback book varies based on size, page count, paper type, and the number of copies printed. For example, a 5x8-inch paperback book starts at around $8.99, while the cost of a larger 8x10-inch paperback book starts at $9.99. Discounts start at 10 copies, with additional volume printing options available. For a custom estimate, try our pricing calculator . How much does it cost to make a hardcover book with Blurb? The cost of a hardcover book varies based on size, cover type, page count, paper type, and the number of copies printed. For example, an 8x10 ImageWrap hardcover book with 70# White Uncoated paper starts at $22.99, while the cost of a 5x8 inch hardcover book with a dust jacket starts at $20.99.
